content.body:
The heaviest AFV in the British inventory at the outbreak of the war, this slow and heavily armored tank was nearly impervious to German anti-tank weapons of the period. The Matilda II used the ubiquitous 40 mm QF 2 Pdr main gun, the standard British Army anti-tank gun of the time. The Matilda II breakout at Arras nearly started a panic in the German ranks until the resourceful General Rommel marshaled FlaK 18's (88 mm guns) from a nearby anti-aircraft battery and was able to knock out the Matildas almost point-blank range. Only the 88 could reliably penetrate the sturdy armor of the Matilda II, otherwise the "Matty" had little to fear from any other contemporary AFV's.
By the campaign in the desert, it had earned the moniker "Queen of the Battlefield" and German tankers showed a distinct reluctance to engage it. Its ponderous speed, inability to be up-gunned, and obvious vulnerability to the 88 meant that its lifespan was limited. After the invasion of Normandy only about 20 were deployed on the continent.
The Matilda is an interesting vehicle to play. A behemoth sometimes able to stop an entire German armored column in its tracks, the Matilda II seduces the player with hints of invulnerability. Don't believe it for a second.
Yes, you are pretty much immune to all German anti-tank guns at the start of a campaign, but later tanks like the Panzer IV G and the StuG III G can kill you easily. The ever-present Stuka can take you out, and, of course, there is always the threat of 88s you can barely see firing from a distance. Audacious gunners know that your gun and tracks are your vulnerabilities, as an immobilized Matilda cannot attack, and a Matilda with a disabled gun is little more than a bulldozer. Relying exclusively on your armor will result in a sad waste of this excellent tank.
Play aggressively but smart. If you have infantry advising of a tank contact, you can drive right over there and take it out, but be alert for ambushes and open spaces where you can be attacked from the air. If you get shot at, don't panic: your armor is good and allows you the time to assess the situation and deal with it carefully. This tank is slow but quite stable, making it an excellent gunnery platform even while moving.
Since your tracks are vulnerable, make sure that when you stop, it is behind low berms or in slight ditches that block line-of-sight to your treads. Really, your only weakness from ground vehicles is the possibility that they can disable your main gun. Do not let even light tanks get a perpendicular view/shot at your gun barrel, point it at them to encourage them to retire, even if you don't shoot them. Better still, park where you are protected from lateral fire while you cover a specific arc and prevent any shots at your gun tube. This is actually good advice for ALL tanks to follow, as disabled guns is a common and a historically worrisome outcome of being spotted by the enemy. Once you lost your gun, in real life as in the game, you want out of there pronto.
Control Variations: The driver spawns in buttoned-up but has a periscope view available (use numpad . or Del key). The driver may also unbutton and drive with his head exposed. The gunner has no view slit. This tanks carries only AP ammunition only and has no range adjustment or gradation available through the gunsight.
